original.target_description: Experiment 1: effect of seven levels of facial redness on perceived anger ratings across angry and neutral computer-generated Caucasian male faces, in the Baruch College participant sample; within-subject redness effect for anger ratings, F(6, 234) = 4.91.

n.sample_role: Participants in Experiment 1 repeated-measures anger-rating analysis; recruited sample retained in the reported test, consistent with the reported repeated-measures degrees of freedom.
n.exclusions: No exclusions reported in Experiment 1 methods/results; forty recruited participants and the reported degrees of freedom support the full sample for this test.
n.location: Article p. 52 (PDF page 4), Experiment 1, Method, Participants; Results, anger-rating redness effect.

es.metric: partial eta squared (η²p; canonical text renders h2p)
es.location: Article p. 52 (PDF page 4), Experiment 1, Results, right column, effect of red on anger ratings.

p.location: Article p. 52 (PDF page 4), Experiment 1, Results, right column, same anger-rating redness effect F(6, 234) = 4.91.

replication.target_description: Unassigned replication side; not examined under original-only blind validation instructions.

notes: Original-only fresh extraction. Published Cognition and Emotion article, volume 32(1), pp. 49–60 (issue 2018; copyright 2016), matching title/authors/DOI in the assigned reference. Visually inspected rendered PDF page 4 (article p. 52) of the named EBSCO PDF. The printed anger-rating partial eta squared is .11; the frozen canonical text drops the decimal and renders it as h2p = 11. The es.value preserves the visually confirmed printed .11; the quotation preserves the canonical text verbatim. This is the omnibus redness effect specifically on anger ratings, not the combined anger/health main effect, interaction, quadratic trend or sex subgroup tests. All three assigned rows have identical original-side study, neutral description and page locator, so the same test is independently applicable. Requested metric is eta squared; the source specifically prints partial eta squared, retained without conversion. Unassigned replication and reported_success are null placeholders; no replication source examined.
